children: By Kim S. Nash

Hello. The federal government's dwindling cybersecurity agency is increasingly seen as a weak link in national security, as ongoing downsizing efforts run up against cyber adversaries armed with advanced artificial intelligence.

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency confirmed plans to shutter a half dozen regional programs that provide security assessments to critical infrastructure operators. Read the full story from WSJ Pro .

Also: We have expanded our CyberIndex of the stock performance of the biggest public cybersecurity companies by market capitalization. For details and an interactive chart showing the activity of each stock in the index, check out the CyberIndex tab at the WSJ Pro Cybersecurity home page. You can also download the data and a PDF of the chart. Let us know what you think.
More Cyber News

Thoma Bravo-backed Proofpoint is in advanced talks to buy cybersecurity firm Varonis Systems, according to people familiar with the matter. Varonis had a market value of around $5 billion as of Tuesday afternoon. Its shares jumped over 10% Wednesday afternoon on news of the discussions, giving it a market value of around $5.4 billion. (WSJ)

Dark web market offers 153 million driver's licenses for sale. The Federal Bureau of Investigation has launched an inquiry into a user offering millions scans of U.S. and Canadian driver's licenses on a Russian underground forum called Exploit. Also available are travel documents, medical cards and other kinds of identification. (KrebsOnSecurity)
The materials came from an ongoing breach at an identity verification company, according to the user on the forum.

Attack on Elon Musk's X platform under investigation. A password-recovery attack against hundreds of thousands of users of X this week has triggered a probe by the Justice Department, Attorney General Todd Blanche said Wednesday. X stopped the attack, Blanche said. (Reuters)

The U.S. has seized more than $560,000 in cryptocurrency donations destined for the Palestinian militant organization Hamas and said that it has taken over a number of websites and servers used to solicit funds and recruits for the group. A group chat claiming association with Hamas on an encrypted communications platform directed supporters to a fundraising website and provided donors with a rotating set of cryptocurrency donation addresses, according to court documents. (Dow Jones Risk Journal gift link)

Amount that kidney dialysis chain DaVita agreed to pay to settle a data breach lawsuit stemming from a ransomware attack in 2025. Hackers stole personal and health information of about 2.7 million people. (Healthcare Dive)
Cyber Business

HiddenLayer raised $100 million in a Series B round led by Delta-v Capital. The Austin, Texas-based startup plans to use the funding to further develop its AI security products, which monitor AI agents for suspicious behavior and identify AI vulnerabilities in corporate tech systems.

Upwind, another AI security startup, is raising about $300 million in new financing, led by Bessemer Venture Partners, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. San Francisco-based Upwind started as a cloud-security provider in 2022 and added AI security capabilities in May.
CISO Moves

Sandro Bucchianeri plans to join Australia's ANZ Bank as CISO on Nov. 11, succeeding acting CISO Shane Ripley. Bucchianeri was most recently group CSO at ANZ rival National Australia Bank. Ripley stepped in after Maria Milosavljevic retired in April, IT News reported.
Sean Bruton joined tech services company Illumia as CISO. He reports to Chief Technology Officer Taran Lent. Bruton was previously CTO at Zyston, a managed security provider.

Grant Yacomeni joined cyber company Gigamon as CISO, reporting to Chief Operating Officer Gareth Maclachlan. Yacomeni spent nearly 10 years at the Defense Department, most recently as chief of the CISO staff.
